accounting.fxPresentation: Ajanta books FX gains in other income and mark-to-market hedge losses in other expenses, gross. FY26: gain ₹97.2 cr, loss ₹103.0 cr (net −₹5.9 cr); Q1FY27: gain ₹50.5 cr, loss ₹30.6 cr (net +₹19.9 cr). Company-reported EBITDA is after the loss; 'adjusted EBITDA' is before it. Screener's annual operating profit is on the adjusted basis and it nets the FY26 loss against other income as an 'exceptional item' (−₹73 cr after tax); its quarterly EBITDA is on the reported basis.
accounting.exceptional: The company reports no exceptional items in FY22-FY26 ('profit before and after exceptional items'). Screener's 'Exceptional items AT' (FY21 +3, FY22 −1, FY23 −6, FY24 +8, FY25 +4, FY26 −73 ₹ cr) are its own reclassifications of FX lines.
accounting.factoring: In FY26 the US subsidiary stopped factoring receivables and borrowed working-capital loans instead (₹212 cr at Mar-26): receivable days 94 → 125, CFO ₹1,157 cr → ₹529 cr; management calls 125 days the 'new normal' and says the P&L effect is neutral (interest cost offset by investment income).

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Ajanta Pharma (consolidated, ₹ crore). Ajanta has no minority interests (all subsidiaries wholly owned; Q1FY27 results note 2), so Screener's Net Profit is profit to shareholders and no patch is needed. Ajanta reports one segment (pharmaceuticals) and sales by market (India branded generics, Asia branded, Africa branded, US generics, Africa institutional), so the engine runs one revenue-growth path and one EBITDA-margin path; the market build sits in `businessLines` and AJANTPHARM.ctx.js checks that it sums to model revenue (AJANTPHARM.mult.js writes revenueGrowth from it). EBITDA margin is the company's 'adjusted EBITDA' basis (before the mark-to-market hedge loss booked in other expenses), the same basis as Screener's annual operating profit; FX gains in other income are not forecast either (net FX assumed nil). Other income = 7.5% on net cash added after Mar-26 + FY26 treasury income on the Mar-26 book + miscellaneous income (built in AJANTPHARM.ctx.js). Valued on P/E, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Built by market (businessLines; AJANTPHARM.ctx.js checks the sum). FY27E: India branded +17% (Q1 +24%, IQVIA MAT Jun-26 +15% vs IPM +11%; guidance 'mid-teens'; 8 launches in Q1, 250-300 reps being added); Asia branded +10% (Q1 −16% as Middle East war disrupted shipping; management expects the deferred shipments in Q2 and cut its FY27 guidance from 'high teens' to 'mid-to-high teens' on 30-Jul-2026; we stay below because the war had not ended by 30-Sep); Africa branded +20% (Q1 +29%; guidance 'high double digit', Q1 'a little higher' than the year will be); US generics +14% in rupees (Q1 +57%, but no launches until Q4; guidance mid-to-upper-mid single digit in constant currency; the rupee was ~₹95/$ in Q1FY27 vs ~₹92 in Q4FY26 per PL's US$51 mn = ₹487 cr; Q2-Q4 need only +3% YoY on a base that included a strong flu season); Africa institutional +15% (Q1 ₹70 cr vs ₹38 cr; lumpy tenders); other operating income flat at ₹45.6 cr. FY28E: India +14%, Asia +13% (recovery from a war-hit base, 15 launches in FY26), Africa +15%, US +4% (price erosion on the eight FY25-26 launches; FY27 filings cut to 5-7 from the 8-12 target in the FY26 annual report), institutional flat. FY29E: India +13%, Asia +12%, Africa +14%, US +4%, institutional flat.

businessLines._why: Sales by market, AR FY26 note 53 (disaggregation of revenue) and MD&A exhibit 1: India ₹1,653.85 cr, emerging markets ₹2,036.56 cr (Asia ₹1,175.0 cr, Africa branded ₹861.56 cr), Africa institution ₹159.82 cr, USA ₹1,557.03 cr = ₹5,407.26 cr from contracts with customers; plus other operating revenue ₹45.60 cr (export incentives ₹25.22 cr, others ₹20.38 cr; AR note 37) = ₹5,452.86 cr.

assumptions._marginWhy: Company 'adjusted EBITDA' (before the mark-to-market hedge loss in other expenses; Screener's annual operating profit is on the same basis): 27.8% FY24, 27.3% FY25, 27.5% FY26, 27.9% in Q1FY27 (−100bp YoY) as gross margin rose to 79.8% (+100bp) but staff costs rose 26% (increments, 300 reps in FY26) and other expenses 32% (new therapies, registrations, freight). Guidance (30-Jul-2026): gross margin ~78% ±1pp, EBITDA margin ~27% ±1pp excluding FX; raw-material inflation from the Middle East war to show from Q2 (Q1 was protected by inventory). FY27E 27.6%: Q1 level less some cost pressure. FY28E 27.8% and FY29E 28.0%: the lower-margin US business falls from 28% to 25% of sales while branded generics grow, partly reinvested in field force and registrations. Each 1pp of margin is ~₹69 cr of EBITDA (~4% of FY28E EPS).
assumptions._capexWhy: Capex ₹330 cr in FY26 (company; Screener cash flow ₹365 cr incl. capital creditors): oral-solid block and liquid plant at Pithampur, a new office in Andheri and maintenance. FY27 guidance ~₹400 cr (30-Jul-2026 call: ~₹300 cr Pithampur expansion for emerging markets, ~₹100 cr maintenance; the 5-May-2026 call split it ₹250 / 150 cr). No guidance beyond FY27: we take ₹350 cr a year (maintenance ₹100-150 cr plus continued capacity), 4.6-5.0% of sales vs 6.6% in FY26.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹173 cr = 5.9% of average gross block (₹2,801 → ₹3,046 cr); Q1FY27 ₹44.5 cr (₹178 cr annualised). The engine depreciates capex at once while CWIP (₹258 cr) is held flat, so 5.7%: FY27E ~₹185 cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied by the engine to opening net cash (₹433 cr at Mar-26 on Screener's basis: cash ₹105 cr + investments ₹588 cr − borrowings and leases ₹260 cr). The FY26 treasury income on the Mar-26 book is carried in otherIncome, so the engine's 7.5% × ₹433 cr is deducted there: in effect 7.5% is earned only on net cash added after Mar-26. 7.5% sits a little below the ~8.1% the debt funds earned in FY26 (₹10.3 cr of gains on ~₹127 cr average holdings, AR notes 15 and 38); the FY26 total treasury yield (₹61.9 cr on ~₹640 cr of average year-end cash and current investments, ~9.7%) is flattered by higher balances during the year and cannot be split from other interest, so we do not extrapolate it.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built in AJANTPHARM.ctx.js from AR FY26 note 38: (1) treasury income on the Mar-26 book (cash ₹103.3 cr, current investments ₹559.9 cr in debt funds, NCDs and commercial paper, bank balances ₹1.5 cr): FY26 interest on investments and deposits ₹51.6 cr + gains on redemption ₹10.25 cr = ₹61.85 cr, held flat; (2) miscellaneous income ₹13.05 cr (FY26); less (3) the engine's 7.5% on the opening ₹433 cr (₹32.5 cr), which would otherwise count the Mar-26 book twice. Left out: FX gains (₹97.2 cr in FY26, ₹50.5 cr in Q1FY27), which are offset by mark-to-market hedge losses in other expenses (₹103.0 cr in FY26, ₹30.6 cr in Q1FY27) that our EBITDA margin also excludes. FY27E total ₹74.9 cr vs FY26 ₹75.0 cr excluding FX (₹172.1 cr reported) and ₹78.5 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26 excluding FX.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 ₹16.1 cr (incl. lease interest on ₹48 cr of leases and the US subsidiary's new working-capital loans, ₹212 cr at Mar-26, which replaced receivable factoring); Q1FY27 ₹3.2 cr (₹12.7 cr annualised). We hold ₹13 cr a year.
assumptions._taxWhy: Effective tax 22.6% FY25, 23.3% FY26, 25.2% in Q1FY27. Guidance ~26% for FY27 (30-Jul-2026); on 5-May-2026 the CFO guided 26-26.5% because a manufacturing facility exits its tax-exemption period. We use 26% for all three years.
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 dividend ₹28 a share (₹350 cr, 33% of EPS); no buyback in FY26 after five since 2019 (₹1,122 cr in all; FY24-25 payout incl. buybacks 76-79%). The Board declared a first interim of ₹32 a share (₹400 cr) for FY27 on 30-Jul-2026, already 34% of our FY27E EPS. We take 35% in FY27E and 40% after, as working-capital needs settle and the ₹1,000 cr in-licensing/acquisition budget (ICICI Direct, May-2026) is not spent in our model.

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash, ~70% of sales from branded generics in India, Asia and Africa (prescription-led, sticky); offsets: 28% of sales in US generics (price erosion, plant inspections), emerging-market currency and war risk. Ke 11.3%, as for Cipla and Alkem.
dcf._tgWhy: 5.5%: branded generics in India and Africa grow ~8-12% a year in value, US generics low single digit in dollars; a blend near 5.5% in rupees.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~10% to 7% by FY42 (India and Africa branded ~9-10%, Asia high single digit, the US flat in dollars).
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 28%: FY29E level held; Ajanta's adjusted margin has been 27-29% in four of the last six years.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex settles at 4.5% of revenue (FY24-26 average 5.5% incl. Pithampur expansion; FY22-24 ~4%); depreciation 3.0% of revenue (FY26 3.2%).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Asia rebounds as management expects (mid-to-high teens) once Middle East shipping normalises, India keeps growing ~1.5x the market with gynaecology and nephrology adding, Africa stays in the high teens, US price erosion is mild and the Q4FY27 launches land, and semaglutide approvals in Asia and Africa arrive on time.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: The Middle East war drags on (Asia flat, freight and API costs up), US prices fall sharply on the recent launches with no new approvals, Africa institutional tenders shrink as donor funding is cut, and India slows to market growth as the cardiology data gap persists.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Ajanta: P/E (MOSL 32x 12-month-forward EPS, PL and ICICI Direct 32x FY28E, BOBCAPS 30x Jun-28E, ICICI Securities 28x FY28E; Jefferies' method not public). 30x Sep-28E EPS = Ajanta's 27.8x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 (house forwardMedian, reported EPS: the company reports no exceptional items; no trough years) x the pharma sector factor of 1.082 (median of the nine-peer set's trailing P/E at the 30-Sep close vs their five-year medians: +8.2% for names outside the set, PLAYBOOK §7c A21) = 30.1x, rounded to the nearest half-turn. Bull 33.5x / bear 25x = 75th / 25th percentile (30.8x / 23.0x) x the factor. No growth, returns or own-move adjustment (sensitivity rows only).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Cross-check. Ajanta's median trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 is 23.1x (Screener); times the EV/EBITDA analogue of the sector factor (+7.5%, PLAYBOOK §7c A21) = 24.8x, rounded to 25x and applied to trailing EBITDA at the target date (half FY27E + half FY28E) with net cash at Sep-2027. Bull 26x / bear 18x = 75th / 25th percentile x the factor.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at an 11.3% cost of equity, terminal growth 5.5%, plus net cash.

cover.headline: A high-quality branded-generics compounder priced for more than it will deliver: the US surge is fading, and at 33.9x FY28E EPS the stock is above its own history even after the sector's re-rating
cover.lead: Ajanta sells first-to-market branded generics in India (30% of sales), Asia (22%) and Africa (16%), plus US generics (29%) and anti-malarial tenders (3%), with ~80% gross margins, 27-28% EBITDA margins, ROCE above 30% and net cash. Q1FY27 was strong (revenue +25% to ₹1,626 cr, profit +31%), but the US, which grew 49% in FY26 on launches, a flu season and a weak rupee, fell 7% QoQ in dollars and is guided to mid-single-digit growth; Asia is hit by the Middle East war. We forecast EPS of ₹95.2 / 106.8 / 119.9 for FY27-29E, below consensus from FY28. Every broker that discloses a method uses **P/E**, and so do we: **30x Sep-28E EPS (₹113.3)**, i.e. Ajanta's 27.8x median forward P/E since Apr-2021 lifted 8.2% for the pharma sector's re-rating, gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL**, a marginal call close to the HOLD line. Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹3,730; DCF ₹2,064. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: #1 in ophthalmology and dermatology in its covered Indian markets, growing ~1.4x the IPM (IQVIA +15.1% vs +11.1%); a rare own-field-force franchise in 21 African countries growing 15-30%; ~80% gross margin; no acquisitions, no exceptional charges, five buybacks since FY19.

arguments.h: But FY26 flattered the US, and that is fading
arguments.p: US sales +48.7% to ₹1,557 cr in FY26 (eight launches in 15 months, a strong flu season); Q1FY27 US$51 mn, −7% QoQ; no launches until Q4FY27; FY27 filings cut to 5-7. We model US +14% in FY27E (rupee-aided) and +4% in FY28E; the street has more.

Operating cash flow halved to ₹529 cr in FY26 as factoring ended (receivables 125 days); the tax rate rises from 23% to ~26%; 14% of the company is pledged by non-executive promoters, one of whom sold 2.8% in Jun-2026; an Aug-2025 income-tax search is unresolved; the MD and JMD take ₹27.5 cr each.

At ₹3,621 Ajanta trades at 39.9x trailing and 33.9x our FY28E EPS against a 27.8x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021, and 14.3% above its own five-year median trailing P/E (pharma peers +8.2%). Our 30x Sep-28E target is in the street's 28-32x range; the gap is our lower EPS. On consensus EPS the same multiple gives a HOLD.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): Asia catch-up from deferred shipments, the US run-rate in dollars, raw-material and freight inflation flowing into gross margin.
US: launches planned for Q4FY27 subject to FDA approval; the Section 232 tariff study (generics exempt until Apr-2027); price erosion on the FY25-26 launches.
Emerging markets: end of the Middle East disruption; semaglutide filings and approvals in Asia and Africa (Biocon licence, approvals ~1.5-2 years out).
Governance: outcome of the income-tax search (block-period return filed 6-Apr-2026); further promoter sales or pledge changes.
Capital allocation: use of the ~₹1,000 cr in-licensing/acquisition budget; second interim dividend for FY27.

sections.title: Five businesses, one model: first-to-market branded generics in India, Asia and Africa, plus US generics and African anti-malarial tenders

blocks.p: Ajanta makes and sells medicines in India and 30-odd other countries. Its core is the **branded generic**: an off-patent medicine sold under Ajanta's own brand and promoted to doctors by its 6,050+ medical representatives. About two-thirds of revenue comes from three such businesses: **India** (₹1,654 cr in FY26; cardiology, ophthalmology, dermatology and pain, with gynaecology and nephrology added in FY26), **Asia** (₹1,175 cr; the Middle East, South-East and Central Asia) and **Africa** (₹862 cr; about 21 countries). The playbook is speed: about half its products were the first of their kind in their market, and it launched 53 products across markets in FY26. The other third: **US generics** (₹1,557 cr, 29% of FY26 sales; unbranded copies sold to US wholesalers from two FDA-approved plants) and **Africa institutional** (₹160 cr; anti-malarials bought by aid agencies). Everything is made in seven Indian plants; there are no acquisitions and no minority shareholders in any subsidiary.

The branded two-thirds compounds at low-to-mid teens; the US third decides whether a year looks spectacular (FY26) or ordinary.

sections.title: From a 1973 repackaging unit to ₹5,450 cr of revenue: a second-generation turnaround, then two decades of organic growth and buybacks

blocks.p: Three brothers, Mannalal, Purushottam and Madhusudan Agrawal, set up Ajanta in 1973 as a small repackaging unit supplying simple medicines to doctors (Forbes India). Before the second generation joined it had made losses for years and carried heavy debt. Mannalal's sons Yogesh and Rajesh took charge in the early 2000s and rebuilt it around first-to-market branded generics: in Indian niches (eye care, skin, heart) and in African and Asian markets where few Indian companies had their own field forces. The US business followed, on two FDA-approved plants. Since then growth has been organic: no acquisitions, five buybacks since FY19, a 1:2 bonus in FY23. Promoter entities have sold stock several times (Jul-2017, Dec-2022, Jun-2026).

sections.title: Industry: India grows ~10%, Africa's private market 7-12%, US generics low single digit with price erosion

Global branded generics: ~US$394 bn in 2025, US$435 bn in 2026, ~10.7% CAGR to 2030 (Research and Markets via AR FY26). US generics: ~US$146 bn in 2025 to ~US$244 bn by 2035, ~5.3% CAGR (Precedence Research via AR FY26). Africa's private branded market grows ~7-12% a year (MD, Q1FY27 call).

blocks.p: Ajanta's India business sold ₹1,654 cr in FY26 (+13.9%) and ₹509 cr in Q1FY27 (+24%). It is a speciality, chronic franchise: 65% of sales are chronic, only 11% are under price control, the top ten brands make 53% and 17 brands sell more than ₹25 cr a year. Ophthalmology is its strongest position: #2 in the IPM and #1 in its covered market (eye drops such as Soft Drops, Bimat and Nepaflam); dermatology climbed from #16 to #13 in a year (Melacare, Salisia KT); in cardiology (Met XL, Cinod), its biggest therapy at 37% of India sales, it is #17. It launched 26 products in FY26, five of them first to market, and 8 in Q1FY27. The field force is 3,750 reps (about 300 added in FY26, 250-300 more planned in FY27); productivity (PCPM) was ₹3.7 lakh a month in FY26 and ~₹4.5 lakh in Q1FY27 (management), with a ₹4-4.5 lakh steady-state target. Gynaecology and nephrology, entered in FY26, were ~2% of India sales in Q1FY27; trade generics (unbranded) were only ₹48 cr in the quarter.

sections.title: Asia and Africa (41% of sales incl. tenders): Africa is booming, Asia is stuck behind the Middle East war, tenders are lumpy

blocks.p: Ajanta sells branded generics in about 32 emerging markets with its own field forces (~2,300 reps outside India), 220+ products and eight therapies. **Africa branded** (₹862 cr, +14.9% in FY26; ₹295 cr in Q1FY27, +29%) is growing far faster than its 7-12% market on launches (8 in FY26, 3 in Q1) and new countries. **Asia branded** (₹1,175 cr, -1.3%) stalled: the war in the Middle East that began at the end of Feb-2026 disrupted shipping (sea freight rerouted, costs up), so Q4FY26 fell 10% and Q1FY27 16% to ₹255 cr. The Biocon licence (23-Dec-2025) gives Ajanta semaglutide for 23 of these countries exclusively (3 semi-exclusive) once approved, which management expects in ~1.5-2 years.

sections.title: Margins: ~80% gross margin, 27-28% EBITDA margin; the FX lines are booked gross, so reported EBITDA understates the business

blocks.p: Ajanta keeps about 79-80 paise of every rupee of sales after materials (gross margin 79.8% in Q1FY27, 78.3% in FY26), because ~70% of sales are branded generics and it makes almost everything in-house. It spends the gross margin on people (staff costs 23.4% of sales in Q1FY27: 6,050+ reps worldwide) and on promotion, registrations, freight and R&D (other expenses 30.3%, including the FX hedge loss). The result has been an EBITDA margin of 27-28% before FX for three years. One accounting habit matters: Ajanta books FX gains in other income and mark-to-market losses on its hedges in other expenses, **gross**. In FY26 the hedge loss was ₹103 cr and the FX gain ₹97 cr: reported EBITDA (₹1,395 cr, 25.6%) looks 190bp worse than the business, and other income looks twice its normal size. We model EBITDA before FX losses and other income before FX gains, i.e. net FX of nil.

FY26 was different: no buyback, a ₹28 dividend (33% of EPS), and cash flow fell to ₹529 cr because the US subsidiary stopped factoring receivables (balance sheet chapter). sections.title: Earnings quality: clean audit, no exceptional items, little capitalised spending; but cash conversion halved and FX is booked gross

blocks.p: B S R & Co. (KPMG) gave an unmodified opinion on FY26. The company reports no exceptional items, expenses all R&D (intangibles only ₹38 cr) and has almost no contingent liabilities (₹8 cr). We flag three things. (1) **Cash conversion:** operating cash flow was ₹529 cr in FY26, 50% of profit (FY25: 126%), because the US subsidiary stopped factoring receivables and funded them with ₹212 cr of loans. Factoring pulled cash forward in earlier years; FY26 is closer to the underlying cash cycle (receivables 125 days). sections.title: Valuation: 30x Sep-28E EPS gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}; the stock already trades above that, at 33.9x our FY28E EPS

blocks.p: Every note standing on 30-Sep-2026 that discloses a method values Ajanta on **P/E**: Motilal Oswal 32x 12-month-forward EPS, PL and ICICI Direct 32x FY28E, BOBCAPS 30x Jun-28E (all 30-Jul to 3-Aug-2026) and ICICI Securities 28x FY28E (per a secondary source); Jefferies does not publish its method. ICICI Direct used EV/EBITDA until May-2026 and switched to P/E in August. We follow the majority: **P/E on Sep-28E EPS (half FY28E, half FY29E)**. Ajanta has no minority interests and reports no exceptional items, so the model's EPS is the right base. EV/EBITDA and a DCF are cross-checks only.

The house rule (PLAYBOOK §4, §7c): Ajanta's own one-year-forward P/E (price ÷ next full fiscal year's EPS) from Apr-2021 to 30-Sep-2026, every fifth weekly close (58 points; house forwardMedian), leaving out trough years (none: the lowest year, FY23's ₹45.9, was 82% of the prior three-year peak); then multiplied by the pharma sector factor for names outside the nine-peer set (the median move of all nine peers' trailing P/E at the 30-Sep-2026 close against their five-year medians: +8.2%, PLAYBOOK §7c A21; our reproduction +8.2%), and rounded to the nearest half-turn. **On exceptional items:** the company reports none; Screener treats the FY26 hedge loss as one (−₹73 cr after tax) while leaving the ₹97 cr FX gain it hedged in profit. We therefore use reported EPS for the base and show Screener's "before exceptional items" EPS as a sensitivity (it gives 30x, the same answer). No own-move, growth or returns adjustment enters the base.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a very good business at a full price; the US normalisation is not in the street's numbers

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** a branded-generics company with ~80% gross margins, 27-28% EBITDA margins, ROCE above 30%, net cash and no exceptional charges; leadership in Indian eye-care and skin niches; a rare African field-force franchise growing 20-30%; and a US generics business that just had its best year. **What you are not buying:** a large Indian franchise (it is #24), pricing power in the US, a hedge against Middle East disruption (Asia is 22% of sales) or a widely held, unpledged shareholder base.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Ajanta Pharma (consolidated, ₹ crore). Ajanta has no minority interests (all subsidiaries wholly owned; Q1FY27 results note 2), so Screener's Net Profit is profit to shareholders and no patch is needed. Ajanta reports one segment (pharmaceuticals) and sales by market (India branded generics, Asia branded, Africa branded, US generics, Africa institutional), so the engine runs one revenue-growth path and one EBITDA-margin path; the market build sits in `businessLines` and AJANTPHARM.ctx.js checks that it sums to model revenue (AJANTPHARM.mult.js writes revenueGrowth from it). EBITDA margin is the company's 'adjusted EBITDA' basis (before the mark-to-market hedge loss booked in other expenses), the same basis as Screener's annual operating profit; FX gains in other income are not forecast either (net FX assumed nil). Other income = 7.5% on net cash added after Mar-26 + FY26 treasury income on the Mar-26 book + miscellaneous income (built in AJANTPHARM.ctx.js). Valued on P/E, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Built by market (businessLines; AJANTPHARM.ctx.js checks the sum). FY27E: India branded +17% (Q1 +24%, IQVIA MAT Jun-26 +15% vs IPM +11%; guidance 'mid-teens'; 8 launches in Q1, 250-300 reps being added); Asia branded +10% (Q1 −16% as Middle East war disrupted shipping; management expects the deferred shipments in Q2 and cut its FY27 guidance from 'high teens' to 'mid-to-high teens' on 30-Jul-2026; we stay below because the war had not ended by 30-Sep); Africa branded +20% (Q1 +29%; guidance 'high double digit', Q1 'a little higher' than the year will be); US generics +14% in rupees (Q1 +57%, but no launches until Q4; guidance mid-to-upper-mid single digit in constant currency; the rupee was ~₹95/$ in Q1FY27 vs ~₹92 in Q4FY26 per PL's US$51 mn = ₹487 cr; Q2-Q4 need only +3% YoY on a base that included a strong flu season); Africa institutional +15% (Q1 ₹70 cr vs ₹38 cr; lumpy tenders); other operating income flat at ₹45.6 cr. FY28E: India +14%, Asia +13% (recovery from a war-hit base, 15 launches in FY26), Africa +15%, US +4% (price erosion on the eight FY25-26 launches; FY27 filings cut to 5-7 from the 8-12 target in the FY26 annual report), institutional flat. FY29E: India +13%, Asia +12%, Africa +14%, US +4%, institutional flat.

businessLines._why: Sales by market, AR FY26 note 53 (disaggregation of revenue) and MD&A exhibit 1: India ₹1,653.85 cr, emerging markets ₹2,036.56 cr (Asia ₹1,175.0 cr, Africa branded ₹861.56 cr), Africa institution ₹159.82 cr, USA ₹1,557.03 cr = ₹5,407.26 cr from contracts with customers; plus other operating revenue ₹45.60 cr (export incentives ₹25.22 cr, others ₹20.38 cr; AR note 37) = ₹5,452.86 cr.

assumptions._marginWhy: Company 'adjusted EBITDA' (before the mark-to-market hedge loss in other expenses; Screener's annual operating profit is on the same basis): 27.8% FY24, 27.3% FY25, 27.5% FY26, 27.9% in Q1FY27 (−100bp YoY) as gross margin rose to 79.8% (+100bp) but staff costs rose 26% (increments, 300 reps in FY26) and other expenses 32% (new therapies, registrations, freight). Guidance (30-Jul-2026): gross margin ~78% ±1pp, EBITDA margin ~27% ±1pp excluding FX; raw-material inflation from the Middle East war to show from Q2 (Q1 was protected by inventory). FY27E 27.6%: Q1 level less some cost pressure. FY28E 27.8% and FY29E 28.0%: the lower-margin US business falls from 28% to 25% of sales while branded generics grow, partly reinvested in field force and registrations. Each 1pp of margin is ~₹69 cr of EBITDA (~4% of FY28E EPS).
assumptions._capexWhy: Capex ₹330 cr in FY26 (company; Screener cash flow ₹365 cr incl. capital creditors): oral-solid block and liquid plant at Pithampur, a new office in Andheri and maintenance. FY27 guidance ~₹400 cr (30-Jul-2026 call: ~₹300 cr Pithampur expansion for emerging markets, ~₹100 cr maintenance; the 5-May-2026 call split it ₹250 / 150 cr). No guidance beyond FY27: we take ₹350 cr a year (maintenance ₹100-150 cr plus continued capacity), 4.6-5.0% of sales vs 6.6% in FY26.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹173 cr = 5.9% of average gross block (₹2,801 → ₹3,046 cr); Q1FY27 ₹44.5 cr (₹178 cr annualised). The engine depreciates capex at once while CWIP (₹258 cr) is held flat, so 5.7%: FY27E ~₹185 cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied by the engine to opening net cash (₹433 cr at Mar-26 on Screener's basis: cash ₹105 cr + investments ₹588 cr − borrowings and leases ₹260 cr). The FY26 treasury income on the Mar-26 book is carried in otherIncome, so the engine's 7.5% × ₹433 cr is deducted there: in effect 7.5% is earned only on net cash added after Mar-26. 7.5% sits a little below the ~8.1% the debt funds earned in FY26 (₹10.3 cr of gains on ~₹127 cr average holdings, AR notes 15 and 38); the FY26 total treasury yield (₹61.9 cr on ~₹640 cr of average year-end cash and current investments, ~9.7%) is flattered by higher balances during the year and cannot be split from other interest, so we do not extrapolate it.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built in AJANTPHARM.ctx.js from AR FY26 note 38: (1) treasury income on the Mar-26 book (cash ₹103.3 cr, current investments ₹559.9 cr in debt funds, NCDs and commercial paper, bank balances ₹1.5 cr): FY26 interest on investments and deposits ₹51.6 cr + gains on redemption ₹10.25 cr = ₹61.85 cr, held flat; (2) miscellaneous income ₹13.05 cr (FY26); less (3) the engine's 7.5% on the opening ₹433 cr (₹32.5 cr), which would otherwise count the Mar-26 book twice. Left out: FX gains (₹97.2 cr in FY26, ₹50.5 cr in Q1FY27), which are offset by mark-to-market hedge losses in other expenses (₹103.0 cr in FY26, ₹30.6 cr in Q1FY27) that our EBITDA margin also excludes. FY27E total ₹74.9 cr vs FY26 ₹75.0 cr excluding FX (₹172.1 cr reported) and ₹78.5 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26 excluding FX.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 ₹16.1 cr (incl. lease interest on ₹48 cr of leases and the US subsidiary's new working-capital loans, ₹212 cr at Mar-26, which replaced receivable factoring); Q1FY27 ₹3.2 cr (₹12.7 cr annualised). We hold ₹13 cr a year.
assumptions._taxWhy: Effective tax 22.6% FY25, 23.3% FY26, 25.2% in Q1FY27. Guidance ~26% for FY27 (30-Jul-2026); on 5-May-2026 the CFO guided 26-26.5% because a manufacturing facility exits its tax-exemption period. We use 26% for all three years.
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 dividend ₹28 a share (₹350 cr, 33% of EPS); no buyback in FY26 after five since 2019 (₹1,122 cr in all; FY24-25 payout incl. buybacks 76-79%). The Board declared a first interim of ₹32 a share (₹400 cr) for FY27 on 30-Jul-2026, already 34% of our FY27E EPS. We take 35% in FY27E and 40% after, as working-capital needs settle and the ₹1,000 cr in-licensing/acquisition budget (ICICI Direct, May-2026) is not spent in our model.

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash, ~70% of sales from branded generics in India, Asia and Africa (prescription-led, sticky); offsets: 28% of sales in US generics (price erosion, plant inspections), emerging-market currency and war risk. Ke 11.3%, as for Cipla and Alkem.
dcf._tgWhy: 5.5%: branded generics in India and Africa grow ~8-12% a year in value, US generics low single digit in dollars; a blend near 5.5% in rupees.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~10% to 7% by FY42 (India and Africa branded ~9-10%, Asia high single digit, the US flat in dollars).
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 28%: FY29E level held; Ajanta's adjusted margin has been 27-29% in four of the last six years.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex settles at 4.5% of revenue (FY24-26 average 5.5% incl. Pithampur expansion; FY22-24 ~4%); depreciation 3.0% of revenue (FY26 3.2%).

Ajanta's median trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 is 23.1x (Screener); times the EV/EBITDA analogue of the sector factor (+7.5%, PLAYBOOK §7c A21) = 24.8x, rounded to 25x and applied to trailing EBITDA at the target date (half FY27E + half FY28E) with net cash at Sep-2027. Bull 26x / bear 18x = 75th / 25th percentile x the factor.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at an 11.3% cost of equity, terminal growth 5.5%, plus net cash.

primary.name: P/E
primary.why: How the street values Ajanta: P/E (MOSL 32x 12-month-forward EPS, PL and ICICI Direct 32x FY28E, BOBCAPS 30x Jun-28E, ICICI Securities 28x FY28E; Jefferies' method not public). 30x Sep-28E EPS = Ajanta's 27.8x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 (house forwardMedian, reported EPS: the company reports no exceptional items; no trough years) x the pharma sector factor of 1.082 (median of the nine-peer set's trailing P/E at the 30-Sep close vs their five-year medians: +8.2% for names outside the set, PLAYBOOK §7c A21) = 30.1x, rounded to the nearest half-turn. Bull 33.5x / bear 25x = 75th / 25th percentile (30.8x / 23.0x) x the factor. No growth, returns or own-move adjustment (sensitivity rows only).
